# 6_coverage_report

Proof that nothing in the source documents was skipped: one report per document cut into pieces (`<document>.md`). It shows that every line of the law is in exactly one piece (or is page furniture: the repeated page title, running header and download footer), and lists each piece with its label and whether an architect approved it (none yet: approval is deferred for now).

**Generated by code only** (`python -m section_labeling coverage`). **Never hand-edit.** CI re-makes it on every change and fails if it differs, or if any line is in no piece or in two.

## residential_districts.md: is each residential district's zoning covered?

Every piece labeled `rule` or `flag` against each of the nine residential districts (R-1a to RU). Each cell says
whether the district's rulebook has a rule for it (which), flags it for review, doesn't need it because the law
keeps it out of the district or it is a pointer with nothing of its own (with the law's words), has it parked (deliberately deferred: Ben's later list, or the brief that parked it), is waiting on an open question,
or is MISSING. It opens with the counts and the MISSING list, ranked, and ends with every rule in each rulebook:
whether model_measurement measures what it needs, and whether a test checks it on a model in `test_data/test_sites`.

What a person decided (why a piece doesn't apply, what is parked or missing) is in `../residential_coverage.yaml`.
Code checks each decision against the rulebooks, the definitions and the law's text before it writes the table
(`packages/section_labeling/section_labeling/district_audit.py`): a rule named as covering a piece must cite it (or
the table says it is Gordium's mapping). A decision that rests on a reading (not applicable, parked, flag) quotes the
law, and code checks only that the quote is the law's own words exactly where it says; it can't check that the
words support the decision. So each such cell is marked [R#], every reading is listed with its quote for a person to
check, and the summary counts the cells that rest on one. **Generated by code only** (`python -m section_labeling audit`). **Never hand-edit.** CI fails if it
differs from a fresh build, so a rulebook change that isn't regenerated fails.

## commercial_districts.md: is each B district's zoning covered?

The same table for the six B districts that have a rulebook (B-1a, B-1b, B-2a, B-2d, B-4, B-5), from the decisions
in `../commercial_coverage.yaml`, built and checked by the same code. Generated by code only; never hand-edit.

## central_business_districts.md: is each CBD district's zoning covered?

The same table for the six central business districts (CBD-50, CBD-60, CBD-85, CBD-100, CBD-120, CBD-140), from the
decisions in `../central_business_coverage.yaml`, built and checked by the same code. A "-" decision names the CBD
column's own cell. Generated by code only; never hand-edit.
